BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Our Buyer Negotiation Playbook. I have treated the Seller's documents as the counterparty's untrusted draft.

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

The preamble says the positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams," are marked FINAL, and are "not intended to be re-opened." It also says 10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are "standard market."

**Recommendation: reject this framing in writing.**
- Our playbook allows the 20% cap and 18-month fallbacks **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies the specific draft. No such authority has been given. Nothing on our side has therefore been "settled" at those levels.
- The "market" assertions are the Seller's advocacy, not agreed facts. They do not bind us.
- Internally, it is worth confirming with Amelia that no informal discussions occurred. Whatever she says, our positions stand until she gives written authority.
- **Tactical caution:** the Seller's 20% cap and 18-month period happen to match our internal fallbacks exactly. Do not signal that these figures are within our authority.

---

## 1. Issue-by-issue departures from the playbook

### A. Liability regime

| Item | Seller position | Playbook | Gap and pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% fallback is unavailable without Amelia's written authority. | Restate 25% / AUD 6.0m. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Five times our position. Reject. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only (a deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket) | Two problems: the amount is five times ours, and the structure is a deductible. The structure matters as much as the number. Reject both. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3/13)** | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia's written approval. | Restate 24 months. |

### B. Hidden general-regime override (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5, "Tax/IP settled", "Fundamental/Title")

This is the most structurally dangerous part of the draft. It works through three linked elements:

1. **"Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."** This is a default override. It would sweep Title, Capacity, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant claims into the general cap, basket, de minimis and time limit unless each one is expressly excluded. If we miss an exclusion, we lose protection.
2. **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature."** As drafted, this would arguably cover **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**.
3. **Title/capacity "subject to the same caps and time limits… for administrative simplicity."** This is a direct departure from the fundamental regime.

**Pushback:**
- Fundamental and Title warranties sit in a **separate regime**: a 100% cap, a period of at least six years, and no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are **carved out of all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable. No one on the deal team should agree otherwise.
- Replace the default override with the reverse rule: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims, and only where expressly stated.
- Keep the Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant and indemnity categories expressly separate.
- **Tax/IP:** the Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not settled. These terms remain **OPEN** on our side. Do not concede that they fall into the general regime. Equally, do not assume or assert that we have secured unlimited liability. Respond only that they are reserved for separate negotiation.

### C. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2])

- [1.1] discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012).
- [1.2] discloses the Accounts, the statutory registers and all "publicly searchable corporate records."

Both are general deemed disclosure, which the playbook rejects.

**Pushback:**
- Delete [1.1] and [1.2].
- Disclosure must be **specific and fair**: identified against the particular warranty, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope.
- The data room can be referenced only where a specific disclosure identifies the particular document and passage.
- Disclosures should never qualify Fundamental/Title warranties or the specific indemnities.

**[1.4] (non-admission):** a non-admission clause is acceptable in principle. Add that it does not limit any indemnity, covenant or Completion deliverable.

**Timing:** the letter speaks "as at" 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Require an updated disclosure letter and data room index. Also require a bring-down mechanism under which new disclosures do not cure warranty breaches or limit Buyer remedies or termination rights.

### D. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

The clause bars any claim for matters known to "the Buyer or its advisers," including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is the broadest form of exclusion. It imputes adviser knowledge and constructive knowledge, and it would undo almost every warranty, given how much the DD has already surfaced (Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-005, DD-006).

**Pushback:** delete it. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it should operate only on **Seller** knowledge, limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### E. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL para 2)

**Why this matters:**
- Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%.
- Clause 11.2 contains a change-control consent requirement, and clause 11.3 attaches conditions to it.
- The Disclosure Letter confirms that no final consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions has been provided.

**Problems with the Seller's position:**
- **"Reasonable endeavours"** is insufficient for a customer of this materiality.
- **"Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent"** treats the condition as met even if Bluefen's 11.3 conditions remain outstanding. A conditional consent could therefore leave the change-control right exercisable after Completion.

**Pushback:**
- Make this a condition precedent requiring an **effective, unconditional (or condition-satisfied) consent**, in a form approved by the Buyer.
- Require **documentary evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion.
- Strengthen the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours, for example to all reasonable or best endeavours, including any cost of satisfying conditions.
- Give the Buyer the sole right to waive the condition.
- Keep the Buyer's termination rights if the condition is not met by the end date.

### F. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL para 3)

**Why this matters:** about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with a change-control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2). The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. A release "to be provided following Completion" means we would complete into live security and a possible change-control default. That is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal.

**Pushback:**
- Require a **current payout letter** from Riverlark as a Completion deliverable.
- Require **direct repayment** from Completion funds, deducted as Debt.
- Require **effective releases** of all security delivered at Completion: deeds of release, PPSR discharges, and return of any share or title documents.
- Confirm whether any Riverlark security extends to the Sale Shares. This ties into the title evidence in item L below.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking** from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists today.

### G. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL para 5)

The Seller says the DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. This is the silent exclusion the playbook warns against. If the Company pays the bonuses after Completion, the Buyer bears them economically. The Disclosure Letter is also silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.

**Pushback:**
- Either show the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a **specific funds-flow line item**, treated as Debt or a Transaction Expense deducted from the price, or have the Seller fund it at Completion.
- Back this with a specific indemnity for any bonus or on-cost amounts not so dealt with.
- Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing. We should not assume a figure either way.

### H. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL para 4)

**What the Disclosure Letter confirms:**
- DD-004 clause 7.3 makes the transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. This is not independent bank verification that the amount is unpaid.
- No receipt or confirmatory assignment has been provided.

**Problem:** an indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers only the fee. It does not cover failure of title to the Project Materials, third-party or Ironquay claims, or the cost of re-creating or licensing the IP.

**Pushback:**
- **Broaden the indemnity** to cover all Loss from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 Project Materials, and any Ironquay claim relating to them.
- **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** a Completion deliverable of either (a) evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory assignment, or (b) payment at Completion from funds flow and a confirmatory assignment.
- Ask for Ironquay's statement of account. The AUD 180,000 is unverified in either direction, so we should neither accept it as owing nor accept that it is paid.

### I. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL para 6)

**What the Disclosure Letter actually says:** about 1,240 records may be in the export. It is not established whether anyone accessed the file, what the exact scope is, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary.

**Problem:** the Seller's cover note goes further and says the incident is "not expected to be material." That is a characterisation the Disclosure Letter does not support. Equally, we must **not** treat it as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a notification duty, or put a dollar figure on it.

**Pushback:**
- Reject any materiality characterisation in the SPA or disclosure.
- Require pre-Completion covenants to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation (forensic where appropriate) and assess notification obligations;
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and consultation rights;
  - take no regulatory or notification steps without consulting the Buyer.
- The disclosure must not qualify the privacy warranties beyond what is actually established.
- Consider a specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident. Frame it without any assumed quantum.

### J. Sandbar renewals (DL para 8)

The Seller calls the three renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000) "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter itself does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Pushback:**
- Assess the renewals before taking a position. Request DD-008 and DD-011 in full, along with termination and notice terms, accrual treatment, and the business rationale for three related renewals.
- Do not accept the "ordinary course" label as a warranty qualification.
- Equally, do not automatically treat the amount as Debt or a price deduction. Decide once the facts are in.

### K. Lease (DL para 7) and Mossvale (DL para 9)

These are not direct playbook departures. However, each disclosure expresses a view that no consent is required. We should verify that independently against DD-007 and DD-009 rather than rely on the Seller's reading. Make the lease notification a Completion step or covenant if it is required.

### L. Title (DL para 10)

The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register. That is a Seller-supplied internal record, not independent proof, and the Disclosure Letter itself acknowledges the Buyer has not verified it.

**Pushback:** require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence:
- current ASIC company extract and allotment and transfer history;
- PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, which ties back to the Riverlark question in item F;
- original or replacement share certificates;
- the constitution, any shareholders' agreement, and confirmation that no pre-emption rights apply or that waivers have been obtained;
- Seller board resolutions authorising the sale, and evidence of the signatories' authority.

Title and capacity warranties stay in the fundamental regime and cannot be qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge.

---

## 2. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing** in writing. We have no authority for the 20% or 18-month fallbacks, and we should not reveal that those are our fallbacks.
2. **Restate the general regime:**
   - 25% / AUD 6.0m cap;
   - AUD 5,000 de minimis;
   - AUD 50,000 tipping (first-dollar) basket;
   - 24-month claims period.
3. **Dismantle the hidden override.** Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims where expressly stated. The Fundamental/Title regime has a 100% cap, at least six years, and no basket or knowledge bar. Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant and indemnity categories remain separate.
4. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of everything.** This is non-negotiable.
5. **Tax/IP remain OPEN.** Do not accept "settled under the general regime." Do not assume unlimited liability either.
6. **Disclosure:**
   - delete [1.1] and [1.2];
   - specific fair disclosure only;
   - an updated letter, given the 22 September cut-off;
   - no cure by bring-down disclosure.
7. **Delete buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** At most, allow a named-person Seller knowledge qualifier after reasonable enquiry, which never excuses title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** a condition precedent requiring effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, a stronger endeavours standard, and Buyer-only waiver.
9. **Riverlark:** a payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs either itemised in the funds flow and deducted, or funded by the Seller, backed by an indemnity.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity to IP ownership and third-party claims, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 rather than assume it is owing or paid.
12. **DD-006:** covenants to preserve logs, investigate and provide updates; reject any materiality label; consider a specific indemnity. Assume no confirmed breach and put no number on it.
13. **Sandbar:** diligence first. No "ordinary course" qualifier, and no automatic Debt or price treatment.
14. **Title:** independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, constitution and pre-emption, authority). DD-012 is not enough.
15. **Lease/Mossvale:** independently verify that no consent is required.

**Escalation note for Amelia Frost:** if the team wants to consider either the 20% cap or the 18-month period, that requires her written authority identifying this specific draft. Nothing in the Seller's papers substitutes for it. Separately, the fraud carve-out cannot be waived by anyone.

- Keep the Buyer's termination rights if the condition is not met by the end date.

### F. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL para 3)

**Why this matters:** about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with a change-control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2). The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. A release "to be provided following Completion" means we would complete into live security and a possible change-control default. That is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal.

**Pushback:**
- Require a **current payout letter** from Riverlark as a Completion deliverable.
- Require **direct repayment** from Completion funds, deducted as Debt.
- Require **effective releases** of all security delivered at Completion: deeds of release, PPSR discharges, and return of any share or title documents.
- Confirm whether any Riverlark security extends to the Sale Shares. This ties into the title evidence in item L below.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking** from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists today.

### G. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL para 5)

The Seller says the DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. This is the silent exclusion the playbook warns against. If the Company pays the bonuses after Completion, the Buyer bears them economically. The Disclosure Letter is also silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.

**Pushback:**
- Either show the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a **specific funds-flow line item**, treated as Debt or a Transaction Expense deducted from the price, or have the Seller fund it at Completion.
- Back this with a specific indemnity for any bonus or on-cost amounts not so dealt with.
- Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing. We should not assume a figure either way.

### H. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL para 4)

**What the Disclosure Letter confirms:**
- DD-004 clause 7.3 makes the transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. This is not independent bank verification that the amount is unpaid.
- No receipt or confirmatory assignment has been provided.

**Problem:** an indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers only the fee. It does not cover failure of title to the Project Materials, third-party or Ironquay claims, or the cost of re-creating or licensing the IP.

**Pushback:**
- **Broaden the indemnity** to cover all Loss from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 Project Materials, and any Ironquay claim relating to them.
- **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** a Completion deliverable of either (a) evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory assignment, or (b) payment at Completion from funds flow and a confirmatory assignment.
- Ask for Ironquay's statement of account. The AUD 180,000 is unverified in either direction, so we should neither accept it as owing nor accept that it is paid.

### I. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL para 6)

**What the Disclosure Letter actually says:** about 1,240 records may be in the export. It is not established whether anyone accessed the file, what the exact scope is, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary.

**Problem:** the Seller's cover note goes further and says the incident is "not expected to be material." That is a characterisation the Disclosure Letter does not support. Equally, we must **not** treat it as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a notification duty, or put a dollar figure on it.

**Pushback:**
- Reject any materiality characterisation in the SPA or disclosure.
- Require pre-Completion covenants to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation (forensic where appropriate) and assess notification obligations;
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and consultation rights;
  - take no regulatory or notification steps without consulting the Buyer.
- The disclosure must not qualify the privacy warranties beyond what is actually established.
- Consider a specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident. Frame it without any assumed quantum.

### J. Sandbar renewals (DL para 8)

The Seller calls the three renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000) "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter itself does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Pushback:**
- Assess the renewals before taking a position. Request DD-008 and DD-011 in full, along with termination and notice terms, accrual treatment, and the business rationale for three related renewals.
- Do not accept the "ordinary course" label as a warranty qualification.
- Equally, do not automatically treat the amount as Debt or a price deduction. Decide once the facts are in.

### K. Lease (DL para 7) and Mossvale (DL para 9)

These are not direct playbook departures. However, each disclosure expresses a view that no consent is required. We should verify that independently against DD-007 and DD-009 rather than rely on the Seller's reading. Make the lease notification a Completion step or covenant if it is required.

### L. Title (DL para 10)

The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register. That is a Seller-supplied internal record, not independent proof, and the Disclosure Letter itself acknowledges the Buyer has not verified it.

**Pushback:** require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence:
- current ASIC company extract and allotment and transfer history;
- PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, which ties back to the Riverlark question in item F;
- original or replacement share certificates;
- the constitution, any shareholders' agreement, and confirmation that no pre-emption rights apply or that waivers have been obtained;
- Seller board resolutions authorising the sale, and evidence of the signatories' authority.

Title and capacity warranties stay in the fundamental regime and cannot be qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge.

## 2. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing** in writing. We have no authority for the 20% or 18-month fallbacks, and we should not reveal that those are our fallbacks.
2. **Restate the general regime:**
   - 25% / AUD 6.0m cap;
   - AUD 5,000 de minimis;
   - AUD 50,000 tipping (first-dollar) basket;
   - 24-month claims period.
3. **Dismantle the hidden override.** Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims where expressly stated. The Fundamental/Title regime has a 100% cap, at least six years, and no basket or knowledge bar. Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant and indemnity categories remain separate.
4. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of everything.** This is non-negotiable.
5. **Tax/IP remain OPEN.** Do not accept "settled under the general regime." Do not assume unlimited liability either.
6. **Disclosure:**
   - delete [1.1] and [1.2];
   - specific fair disclosure only;
   - an updated letter, given the 22 September cut-off;
   - no cure by bring-down disclosure.
7. **Delete buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** At most, allow a named-person Seller knowledge qualifier after reasonable enquiry, which never excuses title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** a condition precedent requiring effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, a stronger endeavours standard, and Buyer-only waiver.
9. **Riverlark:** a payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs either itemised in the funds flow and deducted, or funded by the Seller, backed by an indemnity.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity to IP ownership and third-party claims, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 rather than assume it is owing or paid.
12. **DD-006:** covenants to preserve logs, investigate and provide updates; reject any materiality label; consider a specific indemnity. Assume no confirmed breach and put no number on it.
13. **Sandbar:** diligence first. No "ordinary course" qualifier, and no automatic Debt or price treatment.
14. **Title:** independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, constitution and pre-emption, authority). DD-012 is not enough.
15. **Lease/Mossvale:** independently verify that no consent is required.

**Escalation note for Amelia Frost:** if the team wants to consider either the 20% cap or the 18-month period, that requires her written authority identifying this specific draft. Nothing in the Seller's papers substitutes for it. Separately, the fraud carve-out cannot be waived by anyone.
